newsitem.title: USA: Hemasure to suspend SteriPath program.
newsitem.headline: Hemasure to suspend SteriPath program.

text.p: HemaSure Inc said Wednesday it will suspend activities relating to its SteriPath blood inactivation system, a new technology it is attempting to commercialize for the blood bank market.
In a statement, the company said it took the move after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration raised concerns regarding its use of the chemical hydroxymethylglycinate to neutralize pathogens.
The company said FDA notified it that it could not proceed with clinical trials until all of the agency's concerns were resolved.

"After careful review of the FDA's questions and concerns, we decided that it was in the best interest of the company and its shareholders to suspend activities on the SteriPath program using the HMG compound," said Jack McGuire, HemaSure's newly appointed president and chief executive officer.
The issues the FDA raised concerning the risks and benefits on the use of the compound were "significant," he said.
"To attempt to satisfy the FDA's concerns would require several million dollars and would have a low probability of success," McGuire added.

He said that should another serious pathogen inactivation candidate compound be discovered, whether from inside or outside the company, "we would evaluate how we could combine its use with our filtration capabilities to aid in making the world's blood supply safer."
